A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rationale-Enhanced Decoding (RED) study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable despite reordering and extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, rationale interventions, attention analyses, ablations and hallucination results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds MathVista, MMMU/MMMU-Pro and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The rationale-generation procedure, product of image-conditional and rationale-conditional distributions in Eq. (8), and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Batch-parallel computation is newly documented implementation information; the PDFs do not establish a changed decoding rule.

E1.justification: v2 adds dedicated mathematical reasoning evaluation through MathVista in Table 2 and more complex multimodal reasoning evaluation through MMMU/MMMU-Pro in Appendix B.4. These substantially broaden evaluated reasoning coverage while retaining the original general-reasoning and MMHal/POPE benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including Baseline, CoT, CCoT, VCD, VCD + ICD and the formulation ablations. The added benchmarks use previously evaluated methods. CODE is newly cited but is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New timing protocols measure average inference time per query across benchmarks with Gemma-3-12B (Section 5.7) and milliseconds per token on MMMU/MMMU-Pro with Qwen2.5-VL-7B (Table 7). Existing greedy decoding, backbone configurations and lambda-search settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.7 adds an efficiency analysis comparing RED's parallel dual-forward computation with Baseline and CoT. Existing rationale interventions, capability breakdowns, scaling analysis, qualitative examples, formulation ablations and lambda sensitivity are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. The added timing averages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are unchanged, but v2 substantially expands results across three added benchmarks and timing evaluations. Newly reported Qwen2.5-VL-7B MathVista scores include 70.60 for CoT + RED versus 61.30 for CoT. Table 7 reports RED accuracies of 61.6/40.5 on MMMU/MMMU-Pro versus CoT's 55.5/37.2, alongside timing results. These are new evaluations, not improvements over v1 under retained settings.

T1.justification: The optimal-policy proof now includes rationale r in its state tuple, making explicit the information required by the rationale-dependent reward. The objective, solution and remaining derivation are retained; renaming Proposition 1 as Theorem 4.1 does not itself add a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: existing multimodal CoT underuses rationales, and training-free RED improves rationale grounding and reasoning through a KL-derived decoding rule. Added evaluations support rather than redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes RED's measured latency advantage over CoT to shorter separate contexts under parallel decoding and identifies increased GPU memory use as a limitation. v1 discussed computational cost only as generic inference overhead. Existing rationale-grounding interpretations and broader-impact caveats remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents batch-parallel inference and reuse of the Self-tuned lambda across rationale interventions. It removes v1 Appendix C, including the 24-core Xeon/H100 80GB hardware specification and conditional public-code-release statement. These are changes to disclosed reproducibility information, not evidence that hardware or actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to CODE and MathVista and uses an existing visual-processing reference to justify middle-layer analysis. RED's positioning as a rationale-focused, training-free decoder complementary to hallucination-oriented decoding methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, with corresponding renumbering. v2 also makes limited wording edits, adds an explanatory footnote and new experimental subsections, and removes the reproducibility section. Most existing prose and the overall scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column layout, extensively changing display placement and scale. v2 adds an overview Figure 1 and MMMU/MMMU-Pro Table 7, expands Table 2 with MathVista, and revises several captions. Existing empirical plots and qualitative panels are retained and resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: MathVista and MMMU/MMMU-Pro provide additional evidence for mathematical and harder multimodal reasoning, while Section 5.7 begins to quantify v1's acknowledged inference-cost limitation. The overview figure and implementation clarifications also improve understanding. These gains are tempered by removal of the hardware/code-release statement and sparse documentation of the new evaluations, including unspecified units for Section 5.7's timing values.
